speaker_role: student/recent admit (Caltech), now running a college consulting service with a friend
commercial_incentive: Yes - explicitly promotes paid college support/tutoring/essay review services with 'Olivia' in the video description
key_insights: Non-restrictive plans (regular decision, rolling, early action) let students apply elsewhere simultaneously; restrictive plans (ED, restrictive/single-choice EA) limit other applications
Rolling admission schools review and decide continuously, so applying earlier in the cycle generally improves chances before seats fill up
Early action applicants can see meaningfully higher acceptance rates than regular decision at the same school, per the speaker's cited Harvard example
Early decision is binding: if admitted, the student must withdraw all other applications, and only one ED application is allowed
Restrictive/single-choice early action (e.g. Princeton's REA) is non-binding but limits which other schools can be applied to early, with rules varying by college
Applying early in any form can improve financial aid access since institutional aid pools are less depleted earlier in the cycle

Recommended decision framework: choose ED only for a clear top-choice school, EA when less certain, rolling for safety schools, and regular decision when more time is needed to raise scores/grades or polish essays

For regular-decision applicants seeking a late boost, doing research with a local college professor can yield a strong recommendation letter since research lacks the hard application deadlines internships have
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker cites Harvard regular decision acceptance rate as about 2.57% versus about 7.56% for early action (source/year not stated)
Regular decision deadlines described as mid-December to mid-January with results by late March/early April
Early action deadline cited as November 1st with results by mid-December
Rolling admission results cited as typically arriving in four to five weeks
notable_or_distinctive: Speaker walks through her own real application strategy (safety via rolling, Caltech EA influenced by athletic recruiting contact, Berkeley UC app, Stanford/Harvard regular decision) as a worked example of the framework.
reliability_notes: Ends with a direct pitch for the speaker's paid tutoring/essay/consulting service, which is a commercial incentive to note; the cited Harvard acceptance-rate figures are stated without a source or year and should be verified independently.
